q: Which of the following can a New Cadre (V-B) distributor sell?
e: New Cadre distributors can sell only simple, transparent products: Index funds (Sensex, Nifty 50), large-cap diversified equity, gilt funds, FMPs, equity & gold ETFs, liquid + ultra-short debt. Sectoral, mid-cap, hybrid require V-A.

q: Which of these can a New Cadre distributor NOT sell?
e: Mid-cap, small-cap, sectoral, thematic equity funds require NISM-V-A (full distributor exam). New Cadre is restricted to simpler products to protect retail investors.

q: An Index fund differs from an ETF in that:
o: Index funds trade off-exchange at NAV; ETFs trade on exchange like stocks
Index funds need a demat account; ETFs don't
e: Index funds are bought from / sold to the AMC at end-of-day NAV; no demat needed. ETFs trade on the exchange in real-time with bid-ask spreads; demat account required.

q: A Gold ETF unit typically represents:
e: A Gold ETF unit represents approximately 1 gram of physical gold (or fractions thereof). Held in demat. Lower cost than physical gold (no storage, no making charges) and instantly tradable.

o: Close-ended debt schemes with a fixed tenor
e: FMPs are close-ended debt schemes with a defined tenor (e.g. 3 years). The AMC invests in instruments maturing close to the FMP's tenor, giving investors a predictable yield. Listed but typically held to maturity.
